_comment: Sandbox for the commands crap-gate.py and mutation.py run (qg_common.runCommand). Hooks run outside Claude Code's sandbox with the user's full access (code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing, 'What runs outside the sandbox'), and those commands run code agents wrote. Home only, not overridable from a repo. bwrap: / read-only, the 'hide' paths (the home settings' sandbox denyRead: other homes, the Windows drives under /mnt, /run/WSL whose interop socket would start Windows programs outside bwrap; add a path here whenever one is added to denyRead) and $HOME replaced by empty tmpfs with only the paths below put back, /tmp a fresh tmpfs, no network, a cleared environment. The checkout or scratch copy under test is writable except the 'protect' entries inside it. home_write mirrors the home settings' sandbox allowWrite (uv and Go caches), so a test can't do more than a sandboxed Bash command already can. A repo adds its own protected paths with "protect" in quality-gates.json (read from the diff base, so a branch can't change them); it can't remove these. Known limit: in a worktree .git is a file pointing into the main checkout's .git under a hidden home, so tests or tools that call git (e.g. setuptools-scm) fail and crap-gate only says 'produced no report'.
